svg.title: ReasonAI Mobile architecture: Flutter, Supabase Auth, FastAPI, Next.js, Drift, Nebius ConTree, Nemotron and Tavily
svg.desc: An engineering map of the Flutter mobile application. Its feature shell uses Riverpod and two authenticated Dio transport clients, Supabase Auth and an account-scoped Drift SQLite database. FastAPI handles product data and Knowledge Feed; Next.js handles LangGraph AI chats and server-side Run Submit and reports. Nebius ConTree provides disposable Python sandboxes for mobile execution requests; Nemotron inference uses Nebius Token Factory. Tavily supports bounded research and offline Knowledge discovery. Mobile has no local Python interpreter, no native Konva collaboration canvas, and no completed full offline sync engine.

g.text: Native Flutter UX · authenticated server execution · scoped local state
UI, network orchestration and storage stay in separate boundaries
Two separate Dio clients + auth interceptors
Single refresh retry · owner checks · cancellation
Not the authority for judge results or progress
Backend-owned product truth · Web-owned AI and execution · Supabase identity
Client sends bearer token; services verify
Refresh once; account switch invalidates work
Deterministic ranking; story images via CDN
Durable jobs, private verdicts and AI analysis
Actual mobile routes reach different service pipelines; provider keys never enter Flutter
Model output is parsed, never executed
Public Flutter client: no Nebius, Tavily, R2 or service-role secrets. Mobile judges through the web API, not locally.
Not implemented in Flutter: native System Design/Konva + Go room collaboration, full offline-sync engine, store-release verification.
